project.name: floppy
project.description: Cross-platform (desktop + mobile) peer-to-peer file-transfer app. Tauri 2 Rust backend with iroh transport, SvelteKit + TypeScript frontend, and a Go rendezvous/pairing broker. Devices exchange files directly via code-phrase (PAKE) or trusted-device pairing.

nodes.name: events.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the serde/specta event DTOs emitted from the Rust backend to the SvelteKit frontend (progress, done, error, code, and pairing lifecycle events).
nodes.languageNotes: Every struct derives Serialize + specta::Type so the TypeScript bindings stay in sync with the Rust event payloads.

nodes.name: ProgressEvent
nodes.summary: Payload for transfer progress updates, carrying transferred/total bytes, rate, ETA, and per-file position for the UI progress display.

nodes.name: fileinput.rs
nodes.summary: Resolves and materializes user-picked file inputs (paths, content URIs) into a local cache slot so the transport layer can send them, and reaps stale cache entries.

nodes.name: classify
nodes.summary: Classifies a raw picked input string into a concrete kind (filesystem path vs. platform content URI) for downstream resolution.

nodes.name: resolve_input_path
nodes.summary: Resolves a picked input into a concrete on-disk path, materializing content URIs into the cache directory when needed.

nodes.name: resolve_entry
nodes.summary: Resolves a picked entry into a display name and materialized path, producing the metadata the frontend shows for a queued file.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Tauri application entry point wiring the transport manager, rendezvous, and pairing service into IPC commands, event emitters, deep-link routing, and native notifications.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a specta_builder to generate typed IPC command/event bindings; run() assembles the Tauri Builder with plugins and managed state.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Bootstraps the Tauri application: registers plugins, managed state, IPC handlers, event emitters, deep-link handling, and the async transport/pairing runtime.

nodes.name: specta_builder
nodes.summary: Constructs the specta command/event builder that generates type-safe TypeScript bindings for all backend IPC commands and emitted events.

nodes.name: android_publish
nodes.summary: Android-specific hook that publishes a received file into the user-visible Downloads collection via the platform file-system plugin.

nodes.name: format_bytes
nodes.summary: Formats a byte count into a human-readable size string for notifications and UI display.

nodes.name: resolve_dest_root
nodes.summary: Resolves the platform-appropriate destination root directory where received files are written.

nodes.name: route_deep_link
nodes.summary: Parses an incoming deep-link URL and emits the corresponding DeepLink event so the frontend can act on shared codes or paths.

nodes.name: TauriPairingEmitter
nodes.summary: Adapter implementing the pairing service's emitter trait by forwarding pairing lifecycle events into the Tauri app and native notifications.

nodes.name: TauriEmitter
nodes.summary: Adapter implementing the transport emitter trait, forwarding transport progress/done events to the Tauri frontend and firing completion notifications.

nodes.name: preview.rs
nodes.summary: Custom protocol handler that serves file previews and thumbnails to the webview by responding to permit-authenticated preview URIs.

nodes.name: respond
nodes.summary: Builds the HTTP-style response for a preview request, resolving the file, selecting a content type, and streaming or thumbnailing the bytes.

nodes.name: content_type
nodes.summary: Maps a file extension to a MIME content type for the preview response.

nodes.name: client.rs
nodes.summary: WebSocket mailbox client for the rendezvous broker, joining a room and exchanging wire messages used during code-phrase pairing.

nodes.name: Mailbox
nodes.summary: Handle over a joined rendezvous room providing send/recv of wire messages across the broker mailbox.

nodes.name: recv
nodes.summary: Receives the next wire message from the rendezvous mailbox, decoding frames from the broker WebSocket stream.

nodes.name: code.rs
nodes.summary: Generates, normalizes, and validates short human-readable pairing codes and derives the broker room identifier from a code.

nodes.name: generate
nodes.summary: Generates a fresh random pairing code for initiating a code-phrase transfer.

nodes.name: normalize
nodes.summary: Normalizes user-entered pairing code input into the canonical form used for room derivation.

nodes.name: looks_like_code
nodes.summary: Heuristically checks whether an input string looks like a valid pairing code, used to disambiguate pasted input.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Barrel module aggregating the rendezvous submodules (broker client, pairing code, and PAKE handshake).

nodes.name: pake.rs
nodes.summary: Password-authenticated key exchange (PAKE) handshake over the pairing code, deriving a shared key and sealing/opening the exchanged transport address.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements a PAKE flow so the low-entropy pairing code bootstraps an authenticated encrypted channel for exchanging iroh node addresses.

nodes.name: Handshake
nodes.summary: In-progress PAKE handshake state that finishes into a shared secret once the peer's message is received.

nodes.name: seal
nodes.summary: Encrypts a payload under the PAKE-derived shared key for transmission over the untrusted broker.

nodes.name: open
nodes.summary: Decrypts and authenticates a payload received over the broker using the PAKE-derived shared key.

nodes.name: testsupport.rs
nodes.summary: Test-only helpers that spin up transport managers and in-process mock rendezvous brokers (mailbox and fingerprint) for exercising transfer flows without real network infrastructure.
nodes.languageNotes: Provides mock broker harnesses so integration tests can drive the full pairing + transfer path against an in-memory rendezvous.

nodes.name: mock_mailbox_broker
nodes.summary: Runs an in-process mock of the mailbox rendezvous broker, relaying wire messages between paired clients over local channels for tests.

nodes.name: mock_fp_broker
nodes.summary: Runs an in-process mock of the fingerprint/pairing broker used by trusted-device flows during tests.

nodes.name: test_manager
nodes.summary: Constructs a transport Manager configured for tests with a temporary blob store and deterministic settings.

nodes.name: dest.rs
nodes.summary: Computes the destination path for received files, building a timestamped, sanitized layout under the download root.

nodes.name: receive_dest
nodes.summary: Builds the final destination path for an incoming file, combining the download root with a datetime-stamped, sanitized name.

nodes.name: path_component
nodes.summary: Derives a safe single path component from a candidate name for use in the destination layout.

nodes.name: error.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the transport error types (start errors and coded transfer errors) with stable slugs and default user-facing messages for the frontend.

nodes.name: TransferError
nodes.summary: A transfer failure carrying a machine-readable code plus a human-readable message surfaced to the UI.

nodes.name: TransferErrorCode
nodes.summary: Enumeration of transfer error categories, each mapping to a stable slug and a default localized-ready message.

nodes.name: StartError
nodes.summary: Error type for failures that occur while starting a send or receive before the transfer is underway.

nodes.name: default_message
nodes.summary: Returns the default human-readable message for a given transfer error code.

nodes.name: event.rs
nodes.summary: Internal transport event model (kind, stats, event) plus the Emitter trait the transport uses to publish progress and completion to the host application.

nodes.name: Event
nodes.summary: Transport-internal event carrying a kind and transfer statistics, emitted to the host through the Emitter trait.

nodes.name: manager.rs
nodes.summary: Core transport engine: manages an iroh endpoint and blob store, orchestrating send/receive, quick-share, rendezvous exchange, provider pump, slot busy-state, and cancellation.
nodes.languageNotes: Built on iroh + iroh-blobs; the Manager holds Inner state behind async locks and runs long-lived provider/expiry loops as spawned tasks.

nodes.name: Manager
nodes.summary: Public transport facade exposing send, receive, quick-share/receive, cancel, and busy-state queries over the underlying iroh endpoint and blob store.

nodes.name: Config
nodes.summary: Configuration for the transport manager, including relay settings, download root, and rendezvous broker endpoints.

nodes.name: new_with_publish
nodes.summary: Constructs a Manager, building the iroh endpoint and blob store and wiring the optional platform publish hook for received files.

nodes.name: start_send
nodes.summary: Begins a send by importing files into a blob collection and reserving a send slot, returning the ticket/address for the receiver.

nodes.name: quick_share
nodes.summary: Initiates a code-phrase quick-share: derives a rendezvous room and exchanges the transport address so a receiver can connect with just a code.

nodes.name: quick_receive
nodes.summary: Receives a quick-share by entering the rendezvous room for a code, obtaining the sender's address, and pulling the blob collection.

nodes.name: run_receive
nodes.summary: Drives an in-flight receive, coordinating slot state, event emission, and the underlying blob download.

nodes.name: do_receive
nodes.summary: Performs the actual blob-collection download for a receive, writing entries to their destination paths while reporting progress.

nodes.name: provider_pump
nodes.summary: Long-lived provider loop that serves outgoing blob requests, tracks per-connection progress, and emits send-side events until the transfer completes or is cancelled.

nodes.name: build_collection
nodes.summary: Imports the selected files into the blob store and assembles them into a named blob collection for sending.

nodes.name: cancel
nodes.summary: Cancels an active send or receive, tearing down slots and signalling the associated loops to stop.

nodes.name: rendezvous_send
nodes.summary: Publishes the sender's transport address into the rendezvous room via the PAKE-sealed broker exchange for code-phrase pairing.

nodes.name: rendezvous_receive
nodes.summary: Retrieves and unseals the sender's transport address from the rendezvous room using the pairing code's PAKE handshake.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Barrel module for the transport layer, re-exporting the manager, destination, error, event, and progress submodules.

nodes.name: progress.rs
nodes.summary: Tracks transfer progress and throughput, sampling byte counts to compute a smoothed rate, ETA, and per-file position for progress events.

nodes.name: RateTracker
nodes.summary: Sliding-window rate tracker that smooths byte-throughput samples into a stable transfer rate estimate.

nodes.name: sample
nodes.summary: Records a new byte-count sample and recomputes the smoothed throughput rate over the tracking window.

nodes.name: completed
nodes.summary: Builds the progress snapshot representing a fully completed transfer.

nodes.name: file_at
nodes.summary: Resolves which file within a multi-file transfer corresponds to a given cumulative byte offset for per-file progress reporting.

nodes.languageNotes: Uses tokio-tungstenite split streams and an unbounded mpsc channel to decouple send/receive from the reconnect loop.

nodes.name: identity.rs
nodes.summary: Device cryptographic identity: an Ed25519 signing key plus an X25519 key-exchange key, persisted atomically to disk, exposing fingerprints, signing/verification, ECDH shared secrets, and broker registration proofs.

nodes.name: offer.rs
nodes.summary: Signed transfer-handshake messages (Offer, Response, Completion) carrying an iroh ticket, with canonical byte encoding, signing helpers on Identity, and trust+signature verification against the trust store.
nodes.languageNotes: Deterministic length-prefixed signing bytes ensure signatures cover the exact ticket, guarding against node substitution attacks; includes an inline test module.

nodes.name: sas.rs
nodes.summary: Derives a six-digit short authentication string (SAS) from the ECDH shared secret via HKDF-SHA256, used so two devices can visually compare a code during code pairing.
nodes.languageNotes: HKDF-SHA256 expansion with a domain-separation info string ("floppy/sas") producing a zero-padded 6-digit code.

nodes.name: self_name.rs
nodes.summary: Manages this device's human-readable display name, persisting it to disk and generating a friendly random default name when none is set.

nodes.name: service.rs
nodes.summary: Central trusted-device orchestration service wiring identity, trust store, signed offers, the fingerprint broker, and the iroh transport together: shows/redeems pair codes, sends and receives file offers, and surfaces accept/decline/paired events to the UI.
nodes.languageNotes: Async Tokio service holding Arc/Mutex shared state; a receiver signals its iroh NodeId inside the signed offer so the peer dials only the verified NodeId, removing any shared-secret code from the transfer path.

nodes.name: signal.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the Signal enum (Offer, Response, Completed) exchanged over the broker and its JSON encode/decode helpers.

nodes.name: trust.rs

nodes.name: Incoming
nodes.summary: Enum of events delivered from the broker: a relayed Signal from a peer, or an Unreachable notice when the target device is offline.

nodes.name: connect
nodes.summary: Registers the identity with the broker's fingerprint mode and spawns the background run loop, returning an FpClient plus the incoming-event receiver.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Supervises the broker connection, repeatedly calling serve_once and applying exponential backoff between reconnect attempts until the receiver is closed.

nodes.name: serve_once
nodes.summary: Opens a single WebSocket session to the broker, sends the signed register frame, and pumps outbound signals and inbound relayed messages until the connection drops.

nodes.name: PublicKey
nodes.summary: A peer's public identity (Ed25519 signing key + X25519 kex key) with fingerprint derivation, base64url encode/decode, and verifying-key extraction.

nodes.name: Identity
nodes.summary: This device's private identity: loads or creates persisted keys, and provides public-key export, fingerprinting, message signing, ECDH shared-secret derivation, and broker registration signing.

nodes.name: verify
nodes.summary: Verifies an Ed25519 signature over a message against a peer's public key using strict verification.

nodes.name: verify_register
nodes.summary: Verifies a device's broker registration proof by checking its signature over the canonical register message.

nodes.name: write_file_atomic
nodes.summary: Writes bytes to a temp file with 0600 permissions and atomically renames it into place, preventing partial or world-readable key files.

nodes.name: Offer
nodes.summary: Signed transfer offer carrying the sender's identity, self-name, transfer metadata, and an iroh ticket; verifies trust and its own signature over canonical bytes.

nodes.name: Response
nodes.summary: Signed accept/decline reply to an offer, optionally carrying a decline reason, with trust+signature verification.

nodes.name: Completion
nodes.summary: Signed transfer-completion acknowledgement bound to a transfer id, with trust+signature verification.

nodes.name: sign_offer
nodes.summary: Builds and signs an Offer from an Identity, embedding the transfer metadata and iroh ticket into the canonical signing bytes.

nodes.name: sas
nodes.summary: Derives a six-digit short authentication code from a shared secret via HKDF-SHA256 for out-of-band verification during code pairing.

nodes.name: SelfName
nodes.summary: Holds and persists this device's display name, loading or generating a default on startup and saving changes to disk.

nodes.name: PairingService
nodes.summary: The trusted-device service held in app state: manages identity, trust, broker connection, and transport, exposing commands to pair devices, send/accept/decline offers, and manage trusted devices.

nodes.name: PairingEvent
nodes.summary: Enum of events the service raises to the UI: incoming Offer, Accepted, Declined, pairing Request, Paired, and Error.

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Constructs the service by loading identity/trust/self-name under a directory, connecting to the broker's fingerprint mode, and starting the incoming-signal loop.

nodes.name: show_pair_code
nodes.summary: Generates a pairing code, opens a broker mailbox session, and spawns the task that waits for a redeemer to complete a code pairing.

nodes.name: redeem_pair_code
nodes.summary: Redeems a pairing code by rendezvousing on the broker mailbox, running the PAKE exchange, sealing identities, and adding the peer to the trust store.

nodes.name: send_to
nodes.summary: Starts an outbound transfer to a trusted device by creating an iroh ticket, signing an offer, and routing it to the peer's fingerprint via the broker.

nodes.name: accept
nodes.summary: Accepts a pending verified offer, signs a positive response, and dials the offer's iroh ticket to fetch the incoming files.

nodes.name: decline
nodes.summary: Declines a pending offer by signing and sending a negative response back to the sender.

nodes.name: incoming_loop
nodes.summary: Long-running loop that consumes broker signals, dispatching offers, responses, and completions to the appropriate handlers and updating pending state.

nodes.name: handle_offer
nodes.summary: Processes an incoming offer: verifies trust and signature, auto-declines when busy, and otherwise records it as pending and surfaces it to the user.

nodes.name: surface_offer
nodes.summary: Emits a verified incoming offer to the UI as a PairingEvent and schedules a TTL that drops the prompt if the user never answers.

nodes.name: Signal

tour.title: Project Brief
tour.description: Start here: openspec/config.yaml is floppy's single source of truth for what the project is and how it fits together. It declares the tech stack (Tauri 2 + Rust backend, SvelteKit + TypeScript frontend, a Go rendezvous/pairing broker, and iroh for peer-to-peer transport) and the core idea — securely moving files directly between two devices, either via a short human code-phrase or a persistent trusted-device pairing. Read this before touching code so the rest of the tour has context.

tour.title: Backend Entry & Bootstrap
tour.description: floppy's runtime begins in the Rust core. main.rs is a thin desktop binary that immediately delegates to floppy_lib::run, while lib.rs is the real Tauri application entry point — it constructs and wires the transport manager, the rendezvous client, and the pairing service into Tauri's managed state and registers every command the frontend can invoke. Think of lib.rs as the backend's composition root that every later step plugs into.
tour.languageLesson: Rust/Tauri split the binary (main.rs) from a library crate (lib.rs) so the same core can be reused across desktop and mobile targets. Tauri commands are async fns run on a Tokio runtime; shared services are stored via .manage() and pulled back out with State<T> in each command handler.

tour.title: Rendezvous & Code-Phrase Exchange
tour.description: This is how two strangers find each other with nothing but a short phrase. The rendezvous module joins a room on the Go broker (client.rs), generates and normalizes the human-readable pairing code (code.rs), and runs a password-authenticated key exchange over that code (pake.rs) so a weak phrase bootstraps a strong shared secret without leaking it to the broker. mod.rs aggregates these pieces into the rendezvous surface that lib.rs wired up in Step 2.
tour.languageLesson: PAKE (password-authenticated key exchange) lets both sides derive a strong session key from a low-entropy code while ensuring a passive relay learns nothing and an active attacker gets only one online guess.

tour.title: Transport Engine (iroh)
tour.description: Once peers agree on a secret, the actual bytes flow through the iroh-backed transport. manager.rs is the core engine: it owns an iroh endpoint and blob store and orchestrates send/receive sessions. dest.rs computes where received files land (a timestamped, user-visible location per platform), and progress.rs samples byte counts to report percentage and throughput back to the UI. Together they turn a connected peer into a streaming, resumable file transfer.

tour.title: Device Identity & Trust
tour.description: Trusted-device transfers rest on cryptographic identity. identity.rs (the most depended-upon backend file) gives each device a long-lived Ed25519 signing key plus an X25519 key-agreement key; trust.rs persists the set of paired devices keyed by fingerprint; and sas.rs derives the six-digit short authentication string two users compare out loud to defeat a man-in-the-middle. These primitives underpin everything in the next step.

tour.title: Pairing Orchestration
tour.description: Building on the identity and trust primitives from Step 5, service.rs is the central orchestrator that ties identity, the trust store, and signed handshakes into the full pairing lifecycle. offer.rs defines the signed Offer/Response/Completion messages that carry a transfer handshake, and signal.rs is the enum exchanged over the wire. This is where 'is this device allowed to send to me, and is it really who it claims?' gets answered.

tour.title: The Go Rendezvous Broker
tour.description: The broker is a separate, stateless Go service whose only job is to introduce peers — it never sees plaintext file data. main.go wires up two servers plus a health check: mailbox.go pairs two clients by room id for code-phrase mode, buffering early messages until the second peer arrives, while fproute.go authenticates trusted devices by identity fingerprint and routes signaling between them. This is the server-side counterpart to Step 3's rendezvous client.
tour.languageLesson: Go handles each WebSocket connection in its own goroutine and coordinates room pairing through channels and mutex-guarded maps — cheap concurrency that lets one small process relay many independent transfers at once.

tour.title: The Typed IPC Bridge
tour.description: Now cross the process boundary into the frontend. bindings.ts is auto-generated by tauri-specta and mirrors the entire Rust command-and-event surface as fully typed TypeScript, so the frontend can never call a backend command with the wrong shape. index.ts wraps those raw bindings with runtime shims into the ergonomic IPC facade the Svelte layer actually imports. This generated contract is what keeps the Rust and TypeScript halves of floppy in lockstep.
tour.languageLesson: tauri-specta generates TypeScript types from Rust definitions at build time, giving you end-to-end type safety across the IPC boundary without hand-written glue — rename a Rust command and the frontend fails to compile.

tour.title: Frontend State Stores
tour.description: The frontend's brains are two reactive stores. transfer-app.svelte.ts orchestrates send and receive sessions — queuing files, holding the share phrase, and tracking live status — while pairing-app.svelte.ts manages the trusted-device lifecycle: this device's identity and name, discovered devices, and pairing confirmations. Both call the IPC bridge from Step 8 and expose reactive state the routes and panels render.
tour.languageLesson: Svelte 5 runes ($state, $derived) make plain class fields reactive. Exporting a single instance of a `.svelte.ts` class creates a shared, framework-native store — no external state library needed, and any component that reads it re-renders automatically.

tour.title: Routes & Responsive Shell
tour.description: Steps 8-9's state gets rendered by SvelteKit routes. +layout.svelte wires the one responsive app shell — header, sidebar-on-desktop / drawer-on-mobile, edge-swipe — around every page; +page.svelte is the home transfer surface with send/receive tabs and a mode switcher; and devices/+page.svelte is the trusted-device home where you rename this device, show a code, and manage pairings. One shell tree adapts across desktop and mobile rather than forking per platform.

tour.title: Transfer UI Panels
tour.description: Zooming into the home route, the send and receive experiences are self-contained panels. ModeSwitcher.svelte toggles between them; SendPanel.svelte manages target selection (a shared code or a trusted device) and drives the send flow through its states; ReceivePanel.svelte maps each receive status (idle, connecting, transferring, complete) to the right screen. These panels consume the transfer store from Step 9 and visualize the transport progress from Step 4.

tour.title: Packaging & Mobile Scaffolding
tour.description: How floppy becomes a shippable app on four platforms. tauri.conf.json defines the app identifier, dev/build commands, and window and security settings that bundle the SvelteKit SPA with the Rust core; Cargo.toml declares the backend crate's dependencies (iroh, Tokio, crypto) and build profile; and the Android build.gradle.kts configures SDK levels and the Gradle module Tauri generates for the mobile target. This is the infrastructure that carries everything above onto real devices.

tour.title: The Specs (Brief Closers)
tour.description: Close the loop where you opened it — with OpenSpec. These living capability specs are the authoritative description of intended behavior that the code implements: the Tauri app shell, trusted device pairing, human code-phrase sharing, and the Go rendezvous broker. When code and intent disagree, or before proposing a change, these specs — not the source — are the reference. They tie every earlier step back to the project brief from Step 1.
